title: MLB Brings Its Signature MLBx Format to India for First Time With Suryakumar Yadav
excerpt: After debuting at the All-Star Game in Philadelphia, the 3-on-3 home run competition heads to Mumbai as part of MLB's growing India investment.
body:
• Major League Baseball is bringing its MLBx format — a 3-on-3 co-ed home run competition — to India for the first time, featuring cricket superstar Suryakumar Yadav.
  • The event is part of a broader MLB push into India that includes a partnership with Reliance subsidiary RISE Worldwide and a renewed broadcast deal with JioStar.
  • MLBx debuted on the national stage at the MLB All-Star Game in Philadelphia on July 12, combining former MLB players, softball stars, and celebrity athletes.
  • MLB has been building infrastructure in India since opening offices in New Delhi in 2019, running grassroots programs in schools and youth competitions.

Major League Baseball is bringing its signature MLBx competition to India for the first time, with T20 World Cup-winning cricket captain Suryakumar Yadav set to play a central role in the event, according to an MLB.com announcement.

The move comes weeks after MLBx made its national debut at the MLB All-Star Game in Philadelphia on July 12, where the 3-on-3 co-ed format drew attention for its fast-paced, entertainment-driven approach to baseball. The India event will be part of a live activation in Mumbai planned for October 2026, jointly organized with RISE Worldwide, a subsidiary of Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries.

What Is MLBx?

MLBx — formerly known as MLB Home Run Derby X — is a bracket-style competition that teams a former MLB player, a celebrity or crossover athlete, and a professional softball player. Games run approximately 30 minutes, with players alternating two-minute at-bats and earning points for home runs and catches. Bonus points are awarded through center-field targets and "hot streak" scoring periods.

The format debuted internationally in London in 2022 to build excitement ahead of the MLB London Series. It has since traveled through multiple cities before landing on the All-Star stage this year, where teams captained by former Phillies greats Ryan Howard, Jimmy Rollins, and Shane Victorino competed alongside softball stars from the Athletes Unlimited Softball League.

Why India, Why Now

"India is home to one of the most vibrant sports cultures in the world, and these partnerships allow us to connect with fans in a meaningful way," said Jeremiah Yolkut, MLB's senior vice president of global operations and events, according to Reuters.

MLB has been steadily building its presence in the country since opening offices in New Delhi in 2019. Grassroots initiatives like MLB First Pitch in schools and the MLB Cup youth competition have introduced baseball fundamentals to thousands of Indian students. India-focused original content, including the series Indian Baseball Dreams, has expanded awareness further.

The league's partnership with RISE Worldwide, announced in May, marked a significant escalation. The collaboration spans marketing, social media, and commercial initiatives, with the Mumbai event as its centerpiece.

"For us, it's a long-term play. We're not looking a year out. We're probably looking at 5-10 years out."

— Jeremiah Yolkut, SVP Global Operations, MLB

Suryakumar Yadav's Role

Suryakumar, 35, was named MLB's first Indian ambassador in July. The T20I captain — known as "Mr. 360" for his innovative stroke play — led India to a historic third T20 World Cup victory in March 2026. His crossover appeal makes him a natural bridge between cricket-obsessed India and baseball's global expansion ambitions.

"I'm excited to partner with Major League Baseball and be part of its journey in India," Suryakumar said when the partnership was announced. "I look forward to learning more about the game myself and helping more fans discover the energy, excitement and culture that make baseball something else."

MLB also renewed its broadcast agreement with JioStar, ensuring live games and content continue reaching Indian audiences through one of the country's largest media platforms.

What's Next

The Mumbai MLBx event in October will be the most visible test yet of whether baseball can carve out space in India's cricket-dominated sports market. MLB's strategy mirrors approaches used by the NBA and NFL in international markets — leading with entertainment-first formats before pushing competitive league content.

For the millions of Indian Americans who follow baseball in the U.S., the event represents a cultural bridge — a chance for their adopted sport to gain a foothold in their home country.
nri_angle: The event gives Indian Americans and NRIs a rare chance to see baseball reach their home country, bridging the sport they follow in the U.S. with India's cricket-first culture.
author: Diaspora Desk
